title: The EIA distinguishes high-voltage transmission over long distances from distribution to homes and businesses
summary: The EIA distinguishes high-voltage transmission over long distances from distribution to homes and businesses.
body: The EIA says power plants send electricity to customers through transmission and distribution lines. High-voltage transmission lines carry electricity over long distances, because higher voltage is used for those distances. Utilities operate the distribution system that connects homes and businesses. The source says: "High-voltage transmission lines , such as those hanging between tall metal towers, carry electricity over long distances." Generation, transmission, and distribution are three stages in the EIA's account. A power plant's output is not the electricity measured at a household meter until it has passed through that delivery system, with the losses the system has.
